items.stem: Your age:
Are you currently having menstrual cycles?
If your periods have stopped, approximately how old were you at your last period? (Enter "N/A" if not applicable.)
In the past 12 months, have your cycles become noticeably more variable — shorter, longer, or skipped — compared to your usual pattern?
In the past 12 months, have you skipped any periods of 60 or more days?
Are you currently using any of the following? (Select all that apply.)
Do you have a personal history of any of the following? (Select all that apply.)
options: Blood clot, DVT, or pulmonary embolism

items.stem: Have you ever been formally diagnosed with any of the following? (Select all that apply.)
Are you currently taking any of the following? (Select all that apply.)
options: Stimulant ADHD medication (Adderall, Vyvanse, Ritalin, Concerta, etc.)
Non-stimulant ADHD medication (Strattera, Wellbutrin, Qelbree, guanfacine)

items.stem: If you take any psychiatric or hormonal medication, in the past 6 months how often has it felt less effective than it used to?
Do you have a personal history of any of the following? (Select all that apply.)
options: Heart disease or coronary artery disease
Family history of sudden cardiac death before age 40

items.stem: Have you had thyroid, B12, ferritin, vitamin D, or fasting glucose checked in the past 12 months?
Looking back, were patterns like difficulty focusing, restlessness, disorganization, or emotional reactivity present before age 12 — even mildly?
options: No — these are new in adulthood or midlife

items.stem: When did the cognitive, emotional, or capacity changes that led you here today first become noticeable?
In the past 30 days, have you had thoughts of hurting yourself or ending your life — even passing ones?
In the past 12 months, have you felt afraid of a partner, family member, or someone in your household — or felt controlled by them in a way that limited your choices?
In the past 30 days, has your alcohol or substance use increased in a way that concerns you — or that someone close to you has raised concerns about?
In the past 30 days, have you had any periods of unusually high energy lasting several days at a time, with reduced need for sleep and rapid thoughts or speech?
In the past 30 days, have you experienced sounds, sights, or sensations that others did not seem to experience — or had thoughts that felt forced or placed into your mind from outside?
In the past 90 days, have you noticed an unusually rapid change in your thinking, memory, or awareness — or had moments of disorientation or confusion?
In the past 30 days, have you been unable to complete basic self-care — eating, hygiene, or essential daily tasks — for several days at a time?
In the past 30 days, how often have you started something important the same day you decided to do it?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been able to start a task you were dreading without an external deadline forcing you?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been able to deliver fully on a high-stakes external deadline — even when other parts of your life were neglected to do it?
In the past 30 days, how often have you known exactly what to do and still been unable to make yourself begin?
In the past 30 days, how often have personal tasks that matter to you — your own appointments, paperwork, or health follow-up — sat untouched while tasks for other people got done?
In the past 30 days, how often have you spent more energy avoiding a task than the task itself would have taken?
In the past 30 days, how often have you struggled to act on important things because the payoff or consequence felt too far away?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been able to work on one thing for 30 minutes without your attention pulling somewhere else?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been able to fully tune out your environment and concentrate when you really needed to?
In the past 30 days, how often have you started reading or listening to something and realized minutes in that you’ve absorbed nothing?
In the past 30 days, how often have you lost the thread of a conversation, meeting, or document and had to ask someone to repeat what was just covered?
In the past 30 days, how often has switching between tasks left you unable to remember what you were doing five minutes earlier?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been able to sustain mental effort across the day without crashing?
In the past 30 days, how often have you experienced cognitive fatigue out of proportion to what you actually did?
In the past 30 days, how often has your recovery time after a demanding day or week been longer than it used to be?
In the past 30 days, how often has your mental energy run out before the day’s required tasks were done?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been able to let a small criticism go within an hour of receiving it?
In the past 30 days, how often have you reacted more strongly than you wanted to when you felt criticized, dismissed, or misunderstood?
In the past 30 days, how often has a small frustration cascaded into a much bigger emotional response?
In the past 30 days, how often have you rehearsed a perceived slight or mistake long after the moment passed?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been able to follow multi-step instructions without writing them down or losing the thread?
In the past 30 days, how often have you walked into a room or opened an app and forgotten what you came for?
In the past 30 days, mid-sentence with someone who mattered — a patient, a client, your child — how often has the word you needed simply not come?
In the past 30 days, how often have you forgotten something important until the moment it was needed?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been able to pause before responding when you felt the urge to react quickly?
In the past 30 days, how often have you interrupted someone, blurted something out, or sent a message you wished you hadn’t?
In the past 30 days, how often have you started something on impulse — a project, purchase, or decision — that you later regretted or couldn’t sustain?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been able to break a complex task into ordered steps and follow them in order?
In the past 30 days, how often have important things slipped through because you didn’t have a system to catch them?
In the past 30 days, how often have you stared at a task knowing it was important but unable to figure out where to start?
In the past 30 days, how often have piles of papers, tabs, emails, or unfinished projects accumulated faster than you could process them?
In the past 30 days, how often have you estimated how long a task would take and finished in the time you planned?
In the past 30 days, how often have you lost track of time and arrived late, rushed, or unprepared to something that mattered?
In the past 30 days, how often have tasks taken two or three times longer than you expected?
In the past 30 days, how often has “just one more thing” before you leave or transition turned into far longer than you had?
In the past 30 days, when a wave of heat has come over you in the middle of something — a meeting, a conversation, behind the wheel — how severe has it actually been?
In the past 30 days, when night sweats have happened — whether or not they woke you fully — how severe have they been? (Damp pillow, changed pajamas, woke up overheated all count.)
In the past 30 days, how often have hot flushes or sweats made you step away, change clothes, lose your train of thought, or quietly work around them in ways that took up real space in your day?
In the past 30 days, when your heart has felt different from baseline — racing, pounding, fluttering, or simply too loud at rest — how severe have those episodes been?
In the past 30 days, how severe have headaches been — including any change from your prior pattern in when they happen, how they feel, or what brings them on?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been awake in the middle of the night — alert, mind running — unable to settle back into sleep before the alarm?
In the past 30 days, how often have you woken in the morning feeling that the sleep you got didn’t actually restore you — even when the hours on paper looked fine?
In the past 30 days, how often have you had to actively fight off sleep during the day — in meetings, behind the wheel, sitting down for a moment — even after a full night in bed?
Has anyone who has shared a sleeping space with you ever told you that you snore loudly, gasp, choke, or stop breathing during sleep? (Even if it was years ago, even if you didn’t believe them.)
options: Don’t know — I sleep alone or unobserved

items.stem: In the past 30 days, how often have temperature changes — flushes, sweats, or feeling overheated — been the actual reason your sleep broke?
In the past 3 cycles, how often has your mood, irritability, or capacity dropped sharply in the days before your period and lifted within a few days of bleeding starting? (Time frame: 3 cycles.)
In the past 3 cycles, how often have your focus, sleep, or energy followed a clear pattern tied to where you were in your cycle — sharper at one phase, dulled at another? (Time frame: 3 cycles.)
In the past 12 months, which of the following bleeding changes have you experienced? (Select all that apply.)
options: Periods heavier than they used to be

items.stem: In the past 30 days, how severe has menstrual or pelvic pain been — including pain that no longer tracks neatly with your period?
In the past 30 days, how severe has vaginal or vulvar dryness been in your daily life — sitting, walking, exercising, wearing certain clothes — not only during intimacy?
In the past 30 days, how severe has vaginal or vulvar burning, irritation, or itching been?
In the past 30 days, how severe has discomfort or pain during sexual activity been — at entry, with deeper contact, or after?
In the past 30 days, how severe has urinary urgency or frequency been — sudden need to go, or going far more often than you used to?
In the past 30 days, how severe has unwanted urine leakage been — with cough, sneeze, exercise, urgency, or laughing?
In the past 12 months, how many urinary tract infections have you had?
In the past 30 days, how often have you noticed a clear drop in sexual desire compared to your own prior baseline — not compared to anyone else’s, just compared to you?
In the past 30 days, how severe has difficulty with arousal, lubrication, or physical sexual response been compared to your prior baseline?
If you are experiencing any sexual symptoms, how bothered are you by them — not how bothered you think you should be, just how bothered you actually are? (Mark "Not at all" if no symptoms.)
In the past 30 days, how severe has joint pain been — in your hands, wrists, shoulders, hips, knees, or jaw — including pain that wasn’t there before?
In the past 30 days, how severe has joint stiffness been — in the morning, after sitting, or when you first start moving?
In the past 30 days, how severe has muscle pain or weakness been — including new difficulty with strength tasks (lifting, carrying, opening) you used to do without thinking?
In the past 12 months, have you experienced any of the following? (Select all that apply.)
options: New shoulder pain or restricted shoulder movement (frozen-shoulder pattern)
New or accelerated low back pain
Loss of muscle tone or strength noticeable to you
Bone fracture from a low-impact fall or no clear cause
Diagnosed osteopenia or osteoporosis on DEXA

items.stem: In the past 30 days, how often has your physical energy felt clearly different from your prior baseline — running out earlier, recovering more slowly, or feeling depleted at rest?
In the past 30 days, how often have you needed to lie down, nap, or stop functioning in order to recover from ordinary activity — or had a "next-day crash" you didn’t used to have?
In the past 30 days, how often have you noticed unexplained changes in your body — increased belly fat, muscle loss, or weight that isn’t responding to what used to work?
When did you last have a complete metabolic panel, thyroid panel, B12, ferritin, vitamin D, and HbA1c checked?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been unable to wind down or feel calm — even when you finally had time to rest?
In the past 30 days, how often has your body stayed activated — racing heart, tension, jitteriness — long after the stressful moment had actually ended?
In the past 30 days, how often has irritability or anger shown up in your body — clenched jaw, tight chest, gut tension — before you noticed it in your thoughts or mood?
In the past 30 days, how often have noise, light, crowds, clothing, or smells felt clearly more overwhelming than they used to?
In the past 30 days, how often have you needed to step away, retreat, or physically remove from environments that others around you found tolerable?
In the past 30 days, how often has sensory overload — noise, light, crowds, smells — been the trigger for a mood, focus, or energy crash later in the day or the next day?
In the past 30 days, how often have you noticed your mind working differently than it did 2–5 years ago — in ways that feel like a real change in your baseline, not just stress?
In the past 30 days, how often have your cognitive changes — focus, memory, word recall — felt connected to physical changes like sleep, energy, hot flashes, cycle, or recovery?
In the past 30 days, how often have you felt that something fundamental about how your brain works is shifting — not just that you are tired, stressed, or overloaded?
Compared to your prior baseline, how often in the past 30 days have you needed more cognitive effort to do tasks that used to feel automatic?
